item.title: Trion-mediated quantum operations on a double-dot charge qubit
item.description:
Worth a look theory — Optical pulses to trion states restore resonant tunneling in asymmetric double quantum dots via Coulomb compensation, enabling ultrafast orthogonal single-qubit rotations despite suppressed single-electron tunneling.

Grade 0.457 · 1.9σ above the day's baseline · matched “exchange gates and two-qubit operations in semiconductor double quantum dots” · Alexander Tsukanov

Asks

Can optical excitation to trion states enable fast single-qubit operations in semiconductor double quantum dots with suppressed baseline tunneling?

But

Theoretical model in two dimensions; relies on specific Coulomb compensation of structural asymmetry.

Tools

semiconductor asymmetric double quantum dots · resonant trion state excitation · laser pulse control · dissipative master equation modeling

Abstract

A scheme for controlling a charge qubit on a semiconductor asymmetric double quantum dot with suppressed tunnel coupling between individual quantum dots is proposed. Laser pulses convert the logical single-electron states of the qubit into auxiliary trion states, for which the resonant tunneling condition is restored due to the compensation of structural asymmetry by the Coulomb interaction of the particles. The conditions for performing orthogonal single-qubit rotations are formulated. For a two-dimensional structure, the parameters of the qubit are calculated, and the dependence of the fidelity of the inversion operation on the parameters of the laser field and the rates of dissipative processes is obtained. It is shown that the considered algorithm is characterized by high speed and reliability.

item.title: From NISQ to Fault-Tolerance: Applications and Algorithmic Benchmarks for Spin Qubits
item.description:
Worth a look theory — Compiling Parity Twine to exchange-only (EO) spin qubits reduces the physical exchange-pulse count by more than 22% for QFT and up to 34% for QAOA compared to baseline compilation schemes.

Grade 0.457 · 1.8σ above the day's baseline · matched “Superconducting Qubits: Current State of Play” · Frederik Lohof, Florian Ginzel, Wolfgang Lechner

Figure

Physical exchange-pulse count and Twine/Fowler pulse count ratio as a function of device length L for the quantum Fourier transform.

Asks

How do algorithmic benchmarks and simulation routines scale from NISQ to fault-tolerance when mapped directly to physical exchange-pulse sequences on exchange-only spin qubit QPUs?

But

Analytical and numerical compilation models; assumes single-pulse error rates p≈1.5×10−4, readout error pm≈0.01, and T2≈19.3 μs.

Tools

Parity Twine compilation · exchange-only (EO) spin qubits · pulse-level scheduling with exclusion radius · surface code QEC / lattice surgery error modeling

Abstract

Motivated by recent breakthroughs in the development of spin-based quantum processing units based on exchange-only (EO) spin qubits, we provide a roadmap for the implementation of quantum algorithms on the EO platform, ranging from the NISQ to the fault-tolerant era. To provide an algorithm-driven perspective on the scaling of quantum chips, we consider a range of applications targeting different stages of hardware maturity and formulate requirements for a successful realization. We show that the compilation method Parity Twine perfectly complements the hardware's capabilities to perform tasks such as the quantum Fourier transform or QAOA. Furthermore, we describe an error detection technique native to Parity Twine, which EO qubits can leverage in a unique and advantageous way to improve algorithm performance. Finally, since both near-term algorithmic benchmarks and a long-term perspective can be found in digital quantum simulation, we specifically discuss the fermionic fast Fourier transform and the simulation of Fermi-Hubbard models. The latter is explicitly discussed in the context of quantum error correction and a partially fault-tolerant realization. By providing detailed resource estimates and identifying scaling bottlenecks on each level, our work offers a quantitative perspective on EO-based quantum computing and will inform future hardware design choices.

item.title: Fast universal parametric spin control in an acoustically modulated quantum dot
item.description:
Worth a look new method — Parametric spin control achieves a ∼155 ps Pauli-X gate with average gate fidelity ≥99.9% under uncooled GaAs/InAs nuclear-spin noise and trion lifetime τ≥1.25 ns using ∼44 GHz acoustic driving.

Grade 0.445 · 1.7σ above the day's baseline · matched “Semiconductor spin qubits” · Mateusz Kuniej, Michał Gawełczyk

Figure

Average gate infidelity of the Pauli-X gate plotted against Overhauser noise root-mean-square energy ℏσδ (and dephasing time T2∗) across different acoustic frequencies, trion lifetimes, and harmonic resonances.

Asks

How to achieve fast, universal single-electron spin control in a quantum dot using an acoustic field without being constrained by bare Zeeman resonance and limited rotation axes?

Before

Acousto-optical spin control required resonance with bare Zeeman splitting, was ∼290× slower for noise-mitigating gates, and restricted rotation axes (Ref. 31); all-optical Faraday control was ∼14× slower.

But

Numerical simulations; requires ∼43.88 GHz acoustic driving with 2 meV modulation amplitude (∼2–3×10−4 strain) and trion lifetime τ≥1.25 ns for fidelity ≥99.9%.

Tools

Optically dressed Λ-system in Voigt geometry · Parametric surface acoustic wave modulation · Rotating wave approximation Hamiltonian modeling · Quasi-static Overhauser noise averaging

Abstract

Quantum communication, distributed computing, and hybrid architectures rely on nodes enabling coherent control of qubits and coupling to propagating quantum modes. While semiconductor quantum-dot (QD) spins couple to microwave and optical photons, weak interaction with mechanical waves has limited the integration of single-QD spin qubits into on-chip, acoustically coupled hybrid systems. The existing theory of acoustic QD spin control suffers from a limited range of rotation-axis angles, enforcing complex realizations of gate primitives and long gate times, leaving little margin against decoherence from trion decay and quasi-static nuclear-spin noise. We propose parametric control that overcomes these problems. We use far-detuned optical coupling to a trion state to dress and thus mix spin states, combined with acoustic modulation of the optical transition energy. Instead of relying on direct acoustic resonance with the spin splitting that leads to significant bottlenecks, we induce spin rotations parametrically via resonance with the dressed-spin splitting. We thus develop a spin analog of the ``swing-up'' charge-state excitation. Our scheme provides fast universal qubit control with nearly arbitrary rotation axes. Our ∼155 ps Pauli-X gate duration is ∼290× faster than in the previous acousto-optical formulation and ∼14× faster than optical Faraday-geometry spin rotation. The parametric scheme naturally enables higher-harmonic processes. Numerical simulations for ∼44 GHz acoustic driving show average gate fidelity ≥99.9% even for uncooled nuclear-spin environments of GaAs and InAs QDs for trion lifetime gtrsim1.25 ns. These metrics suggest practically usable control and may introduce a spin-phonon interface with high interaction rates, versatility, and multi-phonon processes, essential for future acoustically coupled hybrid architectures.

item.title: Instantaneous-Frame Theory of Strongly Driven Parametric Gates
item.description:
Worth a look theory — Parametric gates formulated in the instantaneous eigenbasis describe exchange and nonadiabatic ZZ couplings via the non-Abelian Berry connection, matching exact numerical simulations in large-amplitude regimes where idle-frame models fail.

Grade 0.445 · 1.7σ above the day's baseline · matched “Charge-insensitive qubit design derived from the Cooper pair box” · Kentaro Kubo, Shinichi Inoue, Jushin Tei, Yinghao Ho, Yasunobu Nakamura, Hayato Goto

Figure

Population dynamics during a 100 ns parametric iSWAP gate initialized in state |10⟩. In the idle eigenbasis, the state wanders across Hilbert space, whereas in the instantaneous eigenbasis, it undergoes clean two-level Rabi oscillation.

Asks

How can strongly driven parametric two-qubit gates using tunable couplers be accurately and compactly modeled beyond conventional idle-frame approximations?

But

Excitation-number-conserving approximation for leading-order analytical estimates; applied to double-transmon, capacitively shunted double-transmon, and single-transmon couplers with a single flux loop.

Tools

instantaneous eigenbasis representation · non-Abelian Berry connection · Floquet/exact numerical simulation

Abstract

Parametric two-qubit gates using tunable couplers are a promising approach to scalable superconducting quantum processors. However, conventional theories formulated in the idle eigenbasis break down in the large-amplitude regime required for fast gate operations. Here, we show that parametric gates are more naturally and accurately described as coherent rotations between instantaneous eigenstates rather than idle eigenstates. This approach may appear counterintuitive, since instantaneous eigenbases are usually associated with adiabatic dynamics. However, they also form a natural moving frame for driven dynamics, where the non-Abelian Berry connection governs transitions and provides a compact description of the exchange and effective ZZ couplings. We show that this theory achieves quantitative agreement with exact numerical simulations across representative tunable-coupler architectures, including double-transmon, capacitively shunted double-transmon, and single-transmon couplers. The description remains accurate even in regimes where idle-frame descriptions fail, while substantially reducing the reliance on computationally demanding exact simulations. These results establish an instantaneous-frame theory of parametric gates beyond conventional idle-frame models and provide a new perspective on driven quantum dynamics.

item.title: Telecom-Integrated Photonic Memory Operating Near the Mechanical Ground State
item.description:
Worth a look new result — Realized on-chip absorptive optomechanical memory for telecom-band photons operating near mechanical ground state with phonon occupancy nth=0.32 during storage and on-demand retrieval at few-photon level.

Grade 0.440 · 1.7σ above the day's baseline · matched “Cavity quantum electrodynamics for superconducting electrical circuits: An arch…” · Jindao Tang, Bo Jing, Liping Zeng, Peiqin Chen, Hengrui Liang, Yifei Zhang, Xinyao Xu, Qizhi Cai, Xueying Zhang, Qiang Zhou, You Wang, Haizhi Song, Guangcan Guo, Guangwei Deng

Asks

Can an on-chip optomechanical resonator achieve absorptive quantum memory for telecom photons near the mechanical ground state with flexible on-demand retrieval?

But

Measured at 20 mK base temperature with storage operated in the few-photon regime.

Tools

optomechanically induced transparency (OMIT) · nanofabricated mechanical resonators · dilution refrigerator at 20 mK · tailored pulsed optical control fields

Abstract

Scalable quantum networks require quantum memories that are chip-integrated, telecom-band compatible, and capable of flexible retrieval. Nanofabricated mechanical resonators meet these criteria. They offer independent tunability of optical and mechanical modes, long-lived phonon states, and design flexibility beyond atomic systems, making them strong candidates for practical integrated quantum memory. Here, we demonstrate an on-chip, absorptive optomechanical memory for telecom-band photons, based on optomechanically induced transparency (OMIT) and operating near the mechanical ground state. The device stores telecom-band photons, demonstrating compatibility with external photon sources at the few-photon level, while enabling on-demand retrieval. By placing the device in a dilution refrigerator at 20 mK and tailoring the control field to suppress optical heating, we achieve a remarkably low phonon occupancy of just 0.32 during the storage process. Our results lay the groundwork for scalable, phonon-based quantum memory devices and open new avenues for integrating mechanical systems into practical quantum network architectures.

item.title: Preparation of a Bell state in an analogue device hosting the transverse-field Ising model
item.description:
Worth a look new method — Two-step analogue protocol prepares the singlet Bell state |Ψ−⟩ using transverse-field Ising controls alone, reaching infidelity of 2×10−4 at J=1 GHz within ∼100 ns to 200 ns.

Grade 0.438 · 1.6σ above the day's baseline · matched “Charge-insensitive qubit design derived from the Cooper pair box” · Ana Palacios

Figure

State preparation infidelity versus total duration in ns across different coupling strengths J and drive amplitudes ε, showing infidelities below 10−4 at durations under 500 ns.

Asks

Can high-fidelity Bell states be prepared purely via analogue Hamiltonian control in transverse-field Ising architectures?

Before

Gate-based digital Bell-state preparation in superconducting processors takes ∼80–130 ns with infidelity ∼10−3.

But

Numerical simulations in the computational subspace; open-system environmental decoherence omitted; assumes perfect initial state |−−⟩.

Tools

transverse-field Ising model · adiabatic state preparation · resonant population inversion · Hamiltonian engineering

Abstract

We propose a protocol for preparing the singlet Bell state in an analogue device implementing the transverse-field Ising model with ZZ interactions and local X and Z fields, which can be engineered within the superconducting platform, among others. This protocol is performed by direct control of the terms of the Hamiltonian alone. The method exploits the fact that the singlet state is the first excited state of a symmetric Hamiltonian family, and comprises two steps: an adiabatic interpolation preparing the ground state of said symmetric Hamiltonian, followed by the resonant population transfer between its two lowest energy levels. For realistic parameters, the protocol achieves fidelities comparable to standard gate-based preparation within similar time scales (∼100 ns), and can reach infidelities on the order of 10⁻⁴ with a moderately increased duration. We further analyse robustness against systematic control errors and show that high fidelities are maintained under implementation imperfections.

item.title: Robustness of Dynamical Casimir Effect-Induced Quantum Synchronization
item.description:
Worth a look theory — Dynamical Casimir effect-induced qubit synchronization persists under weak cQED dissipation rates, with pure dephasing acting as the dominant limiting mechanism. High Pearson correlation in strong dissipation reflects classical relaxation to a common state, not quantum synchronization.

Grade 0.435 · 1.6σ above the day's baseline · matched “Charge-insensitive qubit design derived from the Cooper pair box” · Sebastián Francisquez, Fernando C. Lombardo, Paula I. Villar

Figure

Pearson correlation coefficient plotted against time for unitary, weak-, intermediate-, and strong-dissipation regimes. Weak dissipation preserves unitary synchronization behavior, while strong dissipation exhibits high Pearson correlation driven by classical relaxation.

Asks

How robust is dynamical Casimir effect-induced synchronization between superconducting qubits against realistic environmental dissipation and decoherence?

But

Theoretical and numerical open-quantum-system simulations within the rotating-wave, Born, Markov, and secular approximations under single-mode cavity and two-level transmon approximations.

Tools

Lindblad master equation · Tavis-Cummings Hamiltonian with parametric DCE driving · Pearson correlation coefficient · Concurrence and Quantum discord

Abstract

The robustness of quantum synchronization induced by the dynamical Casimir effect (DCE) is analyzed within a circuit quantum electrodynamics (cQED) architecture consisting of two superconducting qubits coupled to a shared, parametrically driven cavity. Using a Lindblad master equation approach, this study evaluates the impact of various decoherence channels (including photon loss, relaxation, thermal excitation, and pure dephasing) on the resulting synchronization dynamics. The results demonstrate that DCE-induced synchronization persists under dissipation rates achievable in state-of-the-art superconducting platforms, confirming its experimental feasibility. Among the studied mechanisms, pure dephasing is identified as the dominant factor limiting the fidelity of the synchronized state. Furthermore, it is shown that in strongly dissipative regimes, the Pearson correlation coefficient may overestimate the degree of quantum synchronization, as environmental relaxation can generate classical correlations that mimic synchronized behavior. These findings establish the parameter regimes necessary for observing genuine DCE-induced quantum synchronization and provide practical guidelines for future cQED experiments.
